remediation_steps.step:
Back up the current Terraform file to ensure changes can be reverted if necessary.

Command:
    cp /opt/vuln-labs/cspm-lab/main.tf /opt/vuln-labs/cspm-lab/main.tf.bak-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)

Why: Creating a backup allows for easy rollback in case the changes need to be reverted.

Modify the IAM policy to restrict actions to only those necessary for the workload.

Command:
    sed -i 's/Action   = "s3:ListBucket"/Action   = "s3:GetObject"/' /opt/vuln-labs/cspm-lab/main.tf

Why: Restricting actions to the minimum necessary reduces the risk of unauthorized access and aligns with the principle of least privilege.

Plan the Terraform changes to ensure the modifications are correct and will be applied as expected.

Command:
    cd /opt/vuln-labs/cspm-lab && terraform plan -detailed-exitcode

Why: Running a plan allows you to verify that the changes are correct and will not cause unintended consequences.

Apply the Terraform changes to enforce the updated IAM policy.

Command:
    terraform apply -auto-approve

Why: Applying the changes updates the IAM policy in AWS, enforcing the new restrictions.

Verify the IAM policy changes using Checkov to ensure compliance with security best practices.

Command:
    checkov -d /opt/vuln-labs/cspm-lab --check CKV_AWS_290 --output json --quiet --compact

Why: Re-scanning with Checkov ensures that the policy changes meet the security requirements and that the vulnerability is resolved.

Enable IAM Access Analyzer to evaluate policies and highlight unused permissions that can be removed.

Command:
    aws accessanalyzer create-analyzer --analyzer-name my-analyzer --type ACCOUNT

Why: IAM Access Analyzer helps identify and remove unnecessary permissions, enhancing security by adhering to the principle of least privilege.
